summary: A person may not dig a pit or channel right next to his neighbor's pit unless he keeps it three tefachim away and plasters it. Other things that can hurt a wall, like a mill or an oven, must also be kept a set distance from a neighbor's wall.

chunks.en: A person may not dig a pit
chunks.st: A person may not dig a pit

chunks.en: close to his neighbor's pit,
chunks.st: close to the pit of another, in order to avoid damaging the latter’s pit.

chunks.en: and not a ditch,
chunks.st: And similarly, one may not dig a ditch,

chunks.en: and not a cave,
chunks.st: nor a cave, i.e., a covered pit,

chunks.en: and not a water channel,
chunks.st: nor a water channel,

chunks.en: and not a washing pool,
chunks.st: nor a launderer’s pond, which is a pit used for washing clothes,

chunks.en: unless he moves it away
chunks.st: unless he distanced all of these

chunks.en: three tefachim from his neighbor's wall,
chunks.st: three handbreadths from the wall of another

chunks.en: and plasters it with lime.
chunks.st: and he plasters lime on the place where there is water.

words.note: A white material that seals walls so water cannot leak through.

chunks.en: We keep away olive pulp and manure
chunks.st: And one must distance the solid residue of produce that has been pressed free of its oil, e.g., the refuse of olives from which oil has been squeezed, and animal manure,

words.note: What is left of olives after the oil is squeezed out.

chunks.en: and salt and lime
chunks.st: and salt, and lime,

chunks.he: וְאֶת הַסְּלָעִים מִכָּתְלוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵרוֹ שְׁלשָׁה טְפָחִים,
chunks.en: and rocks three tefachim from a neighbor's wall,
chunks.explain: These things get hot and can damage a wall.
chunks.st: and rocks three handbreadths from the wall of another,
chunks.stMore: as all these items produce heat and can damage the wall.

chunks.en: or he plasters the wall with lime.
chunks.st: Or, alternatively, he may plaster the wall with lime to prevent damage.

chunks.en: We keep away seeds,
chunks.st: One must likewise distance seeds, i.e., one may not plant seeds,

chunks.en: and the plow,
chunks.st: and one may not operate the plow,

chunks.en: and waste water
chunks.st: and one must eliminate urine,

words.note: A polite way to say waste water.

chunks.en: three tefachim from the wall.
chunks.st: three handbreadths from the wall of another.

chunks.he: וּמַרְחִיקִין אֶת הָרֵחַיִם שְׁלשָׁה מִן הַשֶּׁכֶב,
chunks.en: And we keep a mill three tefachim away from its bottom stone,
chunks.st: The mishna continues: And one must distance a mill from a neighbor’s wall by three handbreadths from the lower stone of the mill,

chunks.en: which is four from the top stone.
chunks.st: which is four handbreadths from the smaller upper stone of the mill.

chunks.en: And an oven: three tefachim from its wide bottom,
chunks.st: And there must be a distance of three handbreadths from the protruding base [hakalya] of an oven until the wall,

chunks.en: which is four from its rim.
chunks.st: which is four handbreadths from the narrow upper rim [hassafa] of the oven.

summary: An oven inside a house needs four amos of space above it, and an oven upstairs needs a thick plaster floor under it, so nothing catches fire. If it causes damage, the owner pays, but Rabbi Shimon says that if he kept these measures he does not pay.

chunks.he: לֹא יַעֲמִיד אָדָם תַּנּוּר בְּתוֹךְ הַבַּיִת,
chunks.en: A person may not set up an oven inside the house
chunks.st: A person may not set up an oven inside a house

chunks.en: unless there is
chunks.st: unless there is

chunks.en: four amos of height above it.
chunks.st: a space four cubits high above it,
chunks.stMore: i.e., between the top of the oven and the ceiling, to avoid burning the ceiling, which serves as the floor of the residence above.

chunks.en: If he was setting it up in the upstairs room,
chunks.st: If one was setting up an oven in the upper story,

chunks.he: צָרִיך שֶׁיְּהֵא תַחְתָּיו מַעֲזִיבָה שְׁלשָׁה טְפָחִים.
chunks.en: there must be a plaster floor of three tefachim under it.
chunks.st: there must be a plaster floor beneath it, which serves as the ceiling of the lower story, at least three handbreadths
chunks.stMore: thick, so that the ceiling below does not burn.

chunks.en: And for a small stove, one tefach.
chunks.st: And in the case of a stove the plaster floor must be at least one handbreadth thick.

chunks.en: And if it caused damage,
chunks.st: And if he causes damage in any case,

chunks.en: he pays for what it damaged.
chunks.st: he pays compensation for that which he damaged.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: They did not say all these measures
chunks.st: They said all of these measurements to teach

chunks.en: except to teach that if it caused damage,
chunks.st: only that if he causes damage

chunks.en: he does not have to pay.
chunks.st: he is exempt from paying, as he took all reasonable precautions.

summary: A person may not open a bakery, dye shop or cow barn under a neighbor's storeroom, because the heat and smell can ruin what is stored there. A neighbor can stop someone from opening a store in their shared courtyard because of the noise of customers, but not from making things at home.

chunks.he: לֹא יִפְתַּח אָדָם חֲנוּת שֶׁל נַחְתּוֹמִין
chunks.en: A person may not open a shop of bakers
chunks.st: A person may not open a bakery

chunks.he: וְשֶׁל צַבָּעִין תַּחַת אוֹצָרוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵרוֹ.
chunks.en: or of dyers under his neighbor's storeroom,
chunks.st: or a dye shop beneath the storeroom of another,

chunks.en: and not a cow barn.
chunks.st: and he may not establish a cattle barn
chunks.stMore: there, as these produce heat, smoke, and odors, which rise and damage the items in the storeroom.

chunks.en: In truth, under a wine storeroom they allowed it,
chunks.st: The mishna comments: In truth, the halakha is that in the case of a storeroom of wine the Sages rendered it permitted
chunks.stMore: to set up a bakery and a dye shop beneath, as the heat that rises does not damage the wine.

chunks.en: but not a cow barn.
chunks.st: But they did not render it permitted to establish a cattle barn, because its odor damages the wine.

chunks.en: A store in the courtyard:
chunks.st: If a resident wants to open a store in his courtyard,

chunks.en: a neighbor can stop him and say to him,
chunks.st: his neighbor can protest to prevent him from doing so and say to him:

chunks.en: I cannot sleep from the noise
chunks.st: I am unable to sleep due to the sound of people entering the store

chunks.en: of the people coming in and the people going out.
chunks.st: and the sound of people exiting.

chunks.en: But one may make things at home,
chunks.st: But one may fashion utensils in his house and

chunks.en: go out and sell them in the market,
chunks.st: go out and sell them in the market,
chunks.stMore: despite the fact that he is not allowed to set up a store in the courtyard,

chunks.en: and the neighbor cannot stop
chunks.st: and the neighbor cannot protest

chunks.en: him and say to him,
chunks.st: against him doing so and say to him:

chunks.en: I cannot sleep
chunks.st: I am unable to sleep

chunks.en: not from the noise of the hammer,
chunks.st: due to the sound of the hammer you use to fashion utensils,

chunks.en: and not from the noise of the mill,
chunks.st: nor can he say: I cannot sleep due to the sound of the mill that you use to grind,

chunks.en: and not from the noise of the children.
chunks.st: nor can he say: I cannot sleep due to the sound of the children.
chunks.stMore: It is permitted for one to make reasonable use of his own home.

summary: If someone's wall is next to his neighbor's wall, he may not build another wall close by unless he keeps it four amos away. He must also keep a wall four amos away from a neighbor's windows.

chunks.he: מִי שֶׁהָיָה כָתְלוֹ סָמוּךְ לְכֹתֶל חֲבֵרוֹ,
chunks.en: If someone's wall was close to his neighbor's wall,
chunks.st: One whose wall was close to the wall of another

chunks.en: he may not build another wall close to it,
chunks.st: may not build another wall close to the neighbor’s wall

chunks.en: unless he moves it away
chunks.st: unless he distances it

chunks.en: four amos from it.
chunks.st: four cubits from the wall of the neighbor.

chunks.en: And from windows, above them and below them,
chunks.st: And one who desires to build a wall opposite the windows of a neighbor’s house must distance the wall four cubits from the windows, whether above, below,

chunks.en: and across from them, four amos.
chunks.st: or opposite.

summary: A ladder must be kept four amos from a neighbor's dovecote so a wild animal cannot jump in, and a wall four amos from a roof gutter. A dovecote must be kept fifty amos from the city and from the edges of one's own land, unless it was bought that way.

chunks.en: We keep a ladder away
chunks.st: One must distance his ladder

chunks.en: four amos from a dovecote,
chunks.st: four cubits from a neighbor’s dovecote

chunks.en: so that a mongoose cannot jump in.
chunks.st: so that a mongoose will not be able to jump
chunks.stMore: from the ladder to the dovecote and devour the birds.

words.note: A small wild animal that eats birds.

chunks.he: וְאֶת הַכֹּתֶל מִן הַמַּזְחִילָה אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
chunks.en: And a wall four amos from a roof gutter,
chunks.st: And one must distance his wall four cubits from a roof gutter,

chunks.en: so that he can stand up a ladder there.
chunks.st: so that the neighbor can lean a ladder
chunks.stMore: in the empty space to clean and repair the gutter.

chunks.en: We keep a dovecote away
chunks.st: One must distance a dovecote

chunks.en: fifty amos from the city.
chunks.st: fifty cubits from the city
chunks.stMore: to prevent doves from eating seeds in the town.

chunks.he: וְלֹא יַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם שׁוֹבָךְ בְּתוֹךְ שֶׁלּוֹ,
chunks.en: And a person may not make a dovecote on his own land,
chunks.st: And a person should not establish a dovecote within his own property

chunks.en: unless he has
chunks.st: unless he has

chunks.en: fifty amos in every direction.
chunks.st: fifty cubits in each direction
chunks.stMore: between the dovecote and the edge of his property.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says
chunks.stMore: that one must have surrounding the dovecote the

chunks.en: land for planting four kor of seed,
chunks.st: area required for sowing four kor of seed on each side, which generally extends

words.note: A kor is a big measure of seed.

chunks.en: as far as a dove flies at once.
chunks.st: as far as a dove flies in a single flight.

chunks.en: And if he bought it that way,
chunks.st: And if one bought the dovecote with the land,

chunks.he: אֲפִלּוּ בֵית רֹבַע, הֲרֵי הוּא בְחֶזְקָתוֹ:
chunks.en: even with only a little land around it, he may keep it.
chunks.st: he has the acquired privilege of its use even if it has surrounding it only the area required for sowing a quarter-kav of seed [beit rova]
chunks.stMore: around it, and he need not remove it from there.

summary: A baby dove found within fifty amos of a dovecote belongs to the dovecote's owner, and farther away it belongs to the finder. If it is found between two dovecotes, it goes to the closer one, and if it is right in the middle, they split it.

chunks.en: A baby dove found within fifty amos
chunks.st: With regard to a dove chick [nippul] that was found within fifty cubits of a dovecote,

chunks.en: belongs to the owner of the dovecote.
chunks.st: it belongs to the owner of the dovecote.

chunks.en: Farther than fifty amos,
chunks.st: If it was found beyond fifty cubits from a dovecote,

chunks.en: it belongs to the one who found it.
chunks.st: it belongs to its finder.

chunks.en: If it was found between two dovecotes:
chunks.st: In a case where it was found between two dovecotes,

chunks.en: if it is closer to this one, it is his.
chunks.st: if it was close to this one, it belongs to the owner of this dovecote;

chunks.en: If closer to that one, it is his.
chunks.st: if it was close to that one, it belongs to the owner of that dovecote.

chunks.en: If it is exactly in the middle, the two of them split it.
chunks.explain: That is, it is the same distance from both.
chunks.st: If it was half and half, i.e., equidistant from the two dovecotes, the two owners divide the value of the chick.

summary: A tree must be kept twenty-five amos away from a city, and some big trees fifty amos. If the city was there first, the tree is cut down without payment; if the tree was first, it is cut down and the owner is paid.

chunks.en: We keep a tree away
chunks.st: One must distance a tree

chunks.en: twenty-five amos from the city,
chunks.st: twenty-five cubits from the city,

chunks.en: and a carob tree and a sycamore tree fifty amos.
chunks.st: and in the cases of a carob tree and of a sycamore tree, which have a great many branches, they must be distanced fifty cubits.

chunks.en: Abba Shaul says:
chunks.st: Abba Shaul says:

chunks.en: Every tree that does not give fruit
chunks.st: Every barren tree

chunks.en: needs fifty amos.
chunks.st: must be distanced fifty cubits.

chunks.en: If the city was there first,
chunks.st: And if the city preceded
chunks.stMore: the tree, as one later planted the tree alongside the city,

chunks.en: the tree is cut down, and the owner is not paid.
chunks.st: he cuts down the tree, and the city does not give money to the tree’s owner in compensation.

chunks.en: And if the tree was there first,
chunks.st: And if the tree preceded
chunks.stMore: the city, which expanded after one planted the tree until it reached the tree,

chunks.en: the tree is cut down, and the owner is paid.
chunks.st: he cuts down the tree and the city gives money to its owner.

chunks.en: If we are not sure whether this one was first
chunks.st: If it is uncertain whether this one was first

chunks.en: or that one was first,
chunks.st: or that one was first,

chunks.en: the tree is cut down, and the owner is not paid.
chunks.st: he cuts down the tree and the city does not give money.

summary: A permanent threshing floor must be kept fifty amos from the city, and a person may only make one on his own land if he has fifty amos all around. He must also keep it far enough from his neighbor's plants and plowed field so the chaff does not damage them.

chunks.en: We keep a permanent threshing floor away
chunks.st: One must distance a permanent threshing floor

words.note: A place where grain is beaten and the chaff is blown away.

chunks.en: fifty amos from the city.
chunks.st: fifty cubits from the city,
chunks.stMore: so that the chaff will not harm the city’s residents.

chunks.he: לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם גֹּרֶן קָבוּעַ בְּתוֹךְ שֶׁלּוֹ,
chunks.en: A person may not make a permanent threshing floor on his own land,
chunks.st: Furthermore, a person should not establish a permanent threshing floor even on his own property

chunks.en: unless he has
chunks.st: unless he has

chunks.en: fifty amos in every direction,
chunks.st: fifty cubits of open space in every direction.

chunks.en: and he keeps it away from his neighbor's plants and plowed field,
chunks.st: And one must distance a threshing floor from the plantings of another and from another’s plowed field far

chunks.en: so that it will not cause damage.
chunks.st: enough that it does not cause damage.

summary: Animal carcasses, graves and a tannery, where smelly hides are worked, must be kept fifty amos from a city. The tannery must be on the east side of the city, and Rabbi Akiva says it may be on any side except the west.

chunks.en: We keep away dead animals,
chunks.st: One must distance animal carcasses,

chunks.en: and graves,
chunks.st: and graves,

chunks.en: and a tannery,
chunks.st: and a tannery [haburseki], a place where hides are processed,

words.note: A place where animal skins are made into leather. It smells bad.

chunks.en: fifty amos from the city.
chunks.st: fifty cubits from the city.

chunks.he: אֵין עוֹשִׂין בֻּרְסְקִי אֶלָּא לְמִזְרַח הָעִיר.
chunks.en: We make a tannery only on the east side of the city.
chunks.explain: The wind usually blows the smell away from the city.
chunks.st: One may establish a tannery only on the east side of the city,
chunks.stMore: because winds usually blow from the west and the foul smells would therefore be blown away from the residential area.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: He may make it on any side,
chunks.st: One may establish a tannery on any side of a city

chunks.en: except the west side,
chunks.st: except for the west,
chunks.stMore: as the winds blowing from that direction will bring the odors into the city,

chunks.en: and he keeps it fifty amos away.
chunks.st: and one must distance it fifty cubits from the city.

summary: Some things harm the things near them, so they must be kept apart: flax-soaking water from vegetables, leeks from onions, and mustard from bees. Rabbi Yosei allows mustard to stay near bees.

chunks.en: We keep flax-soaking water away from vegetables,
chunks.st: One must distance from vegetables water in which flax is steeped, because this water ruins them;

words.note: Water where flax is soaked. It ruins vegetables.

chunks.en: and leeks from onions,
chunks.st: and likewise one must distance leeks from onions,

chunks.en: and mustard from bees.
chunks.st: and mustard from bees.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei allows it with mustard.
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yosei permits one not to do so in the case of mustard.

summary: A tree must be kept twenty-five amos from a neighbor's cistern, and some big trees fifty amos, because roots can damage it. Who has to cut the tree depends on which came first, and Rabbi Yosei says the tree never has to be cut, because each one is using his own land.

chunks.en: We keep a tree away
chunks.st: One must distance a tree

chunks.en: twenty-five amos from a cistern,
chunks.st: twenty-five cubits from a cistern,

chunks.en: and a carob or sycamore tree fifty amos,
chunks.st: and in the case of a carob and of a sycamore tree, whose roots extend farther, one must distance the tree fifty cubits.

chunks.en: whether it is above it or to the side.
chunks.st: This is the halakha whether the cistern or tree is located above or to the side of the other.

chunks.en: If the cistern came first,
chunks.st: If the digging of the cistern preceded the tree,

chunks.en: he cuts down the tree, and the cistern owner pays for it.
chunks.st: the owner of the tree cuts down the tree and the owner of the cistern pays him money.

chunks.en: And if the tree came first,
chunks.st: And if the tree preceded the cistern

chunks.en: he does not cut it down.
chunks.st: the owner of the tree need not cut down the tree.

chunks.en: If we are not sure whether this one came first
chunks.st: If it is uncertain whether this came first

chunks.en: or that one came first,
chunks.st: or that came first,

chunks.en: he does not cut it down.
chunks.st: the owner of the tree need not cut down the tree.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַבּוֹר קוֹדֶמֶת לָאִילָן,
chunks.en: Even if the cistern came before the tree,
chunks.st: Even if the cistern preceded the tree,

chunks.en: he does not cut it down,
chunks.st: the owner of the tree need not cut down the tree.

chunks.en: because this one digs in his own land,
chunks.st: This is due to the fact that this one digs in his own property,

chunks.en: and that one plants in his own land.
chunks.st: and that one plants in his own property.

summary: A person must plant his trees four amos away from his neighbor's field, unless there is a fence between them. If a tree's roots grow into the neighbor's field, the neighbor may cut them when he plows or digs.

chunks.en: A person may not plant a tree
chunks.st: A person may not plant a tree

chunks.en: close to his neighbor's field,
chunks.st: near the field of another

chunks.en: unless he moves it away
chunks.st: unless he distances it

chunks.en: four amos from it,
chunks.st: four cubits from the field.

chunks.en: whether grapevines or any tree.
chunks.st: This is the case whether he is planting grapevines or any kind of tree.

chunks.en: If there was a fence in between,
chunks.st: If there was a fence between them,

chunks.en: this one may plant close to the fence on this side,
chunks.st: this one may place, i.e., plant, his grapevines or trees close to the fence from here,

chunks.en: and that one close to the fence on that side.
chunks.st: and that one may place, i.e., plant, his produce close to the fence from there.

chunks.he: הָיוּ שָׁרָשִׁים יוֹצְאִין לְתוֹךְ שֶׁל חֲבֵרוֹ,
chunks.en: If roots were going into his neighbor's field,
chunks.st: If the roots were spreading into the field of another,

chunks.en: the neighbor digs down three tefachim,
chunks.explain: He may cut off the roots in his way.
chunks.st: the owner of the field may dig to a depth of three handbreadths even if he severs those roots,

chunks.en: so that they will not get in the way of the plow.
chunks.st: so that they do not impede his plow.

chunks.en: If he was digging a pit,
chunks.st: If he was digging a cistern in that spot,

chunks.en: a ditch or a cave,
chunks.st: or a ditch, or a cave,

chunks.en: he cuts the roots and goes down,
chunks.st: and he came upon the roots of his neighbor’s tree, he may cut downward normally,

chunks.en: and the wood is his.
chunks.st: and the wood from the roots is his.

summary: If a neighbor's tree leans over a field, the field owner may cut the branches so his plow can pass under. For trees with lots of shade, or over a watered field, he may cut everything that hangs over his side.

chunks.en: A tree that leans over a neighbor's field:
chunks.st: With regard to a tree that leans into the field of another,

chunks.he: קוֹצֵץ מְלֹא הַמַּרְדֵּעַ עַל גַּבֵּי הַמַּחֲרֵשָׁה.
chunks.en: he cuts it as high as an ox stick held above the plow.
chunks.st: the neighbor may cut the branches to the height of an ox goad raised over the plow,
chunks.stMore: in places where the land is to be plowed, so that the branches do not impede the use of the plow.

words.note: A long stick used to drive oxen.

chunks.en: And with a carob tree or a sycamore tree,
chunks.st: And in the case of a carob tree and the case of a sycamore tree,
chunks.stMore: whose abundance of branches cast shade that is harmful to plants,

chunks.en: he cuts straight up along the border line.
chunks.st: all the branches overhanging one’s property may be removed along the plumb line,
chunks.stMore: i.e., along a line perpendicular to the boundary separating the fields.

words.note: A string with a weight that hangs straight down.

chunks.en: With a field that needs watering,
chunks.st: And if the neighbor’s field is an irrigated field,

chunks.en: every tree is cut straight up along the line.
chunks.st: all branches of the tree are removed along the plumb line.

chunks.en: Abba Shaul says:
chunks.st: Abba Shaul says:

chunks.en: Every tree that does not give fruit
chunks.st: All barren trees

chunks.en: is cut straight up along the line.
chunks.st: are cut along the plumb line.

summary: Branches of a tree that hang over a public road are cut so that a camel with its rider can pass. Rabbi Shimon says every branch over the road is cut, so that people walking underneath do not become tamei.

chunks.en: A tree that leans over a public road:
chunks.st: With regard to a tree that extends into the public domain,

words.note: The public area, like a street.

chunks.he: קוֹצֵץ, כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא גָמָל עוֹבֵר וְרוֹכְבוֹ.
chunks.en: he cuts it so that a camel can pass with its rider.
chunks.st: one cuts its branches so that a camel can pass beneath the tree with its rider sitting on it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.he: גָּמָל טָעוּן פִּשְׁתָּן אוֹ חֲבִילֵי זְמוֹרוֹת.
chunks.en: So that a camel loaded with flax or bundles of branches can pass.
chunks.st: One cuts enough branches that a camel loaded with flax or bundles of branches can pass beneath it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: Every tree is cut straight up along the line,
chunks.st: One cuts all branches of the tree that extend into the public domain along the plumb line,
chunks.stMore: so that they do not hang over the public area at all,

chunks.en: because of tumah.
chunks.explain: A branch over something tamei can make people under it tamei.
chunks.st: due to ritual impurity.
